element: Snelleman et al. (Automated Reproducibility Has a Problem Statement Problem, RAI/ReproAI Workshop @ AAAI 2026)

UC1.note: Output is a hypotheses/experiments/interpretations graph, not a venue-format artifact appendix.

UC3.evidence: "correct any mistakes made by the LLM in its phrasings, links between hypotheses, experiments and interpretations, as well as experiment details, such as measured outcomes" (Method, p.3); Table 2 lists 'Experiment Hypothesis links', 'Interpretation Experiment links' (p.4)
UC3.note: Links are paper-internal (hypothesis->experiment->result), never to artifact files/scripts; 1 is defensible only as the claim-side half of L, 0 is also arguable.

UC4.note: The artifact/repo is never read; input is the PDF only.

UC5.evidence: "in some cases, a clear phrasing of hypotheses or research questions within a given study is essential for capturing the essence of the work" (Discussion, p.5)
UC5.note: Extraction failures are observed as a limitation of the method, not reported to users as paper gaps; no deliverable on paper underspecification.

UC6.evidence: "automatically extract the problem statement of reproducibility for any empirical AI study" (Introduction, p.1)
UC6.note: The extracted structure is meant as input to reproduction agents, not as code/env/docs artifact material; 0 stands but a generous reader could call it a structured doc from P.

UC8.note: Related papers are only discussed in the Related Work section; the tool does not link papers.

B1.evidence: "In order to relieve independent investigators of the workload, the automatisation of reproducing studies to any extent would have a substantial impact." (Introduction, p.1)
B1.note: Intended consumer is an independent reproducer / automated reproducibility agent, not the original author; authors only served as ground-truth raters. Current 3 is defensible as 'neither', 4 fits better.

B2.evidence: "We constructed a relatively simple prompt and presented this, together with the PDF of each publication, to Google Gemini 2.5 Pro" (Method, p.3)

B3.evidence: "We applied our representation to automatically extract the problem from any PDF and reviewed its capabilities on 20 studies" (Conclusion, p.5)

B4.evidence: "We consider the following notion of reproducibility, based on Gundersen (2021) ... we derive our problem statement, formulated in terms of the scientific method" (Background, p.3)
B4.note: Driven by the authors' own scientific-method schema, not a venue standard; 2 is arguable given reliance on Gundersen 2021's published definition.

B5.evidence: "prompted the model to produce the hypotheses, experiments and interpretations of outcomes for the 20 publications" (Method, p.3); "Authors were given the opportunity to adapt the phrasing." (Fig. 5 caption, p.4)
B5.note: Emits a structured graph of textual statements and links, not a score; 4 (structured document, not free prose) is reasonable.

disagreements: B1: current 3, should be 4 because the stated beneficiary is the independent investigator / automated reproduction agent (evaluator side), and original authors appear only as raters of extraction quality, never as intended users.
one_line_summary: Gemini 2.5 Pro extracts a hypotheses-experiments-results-interpretations graph from a paper PDF as a generalisable problem statement for automated reproduction; 20 papers' authors rated the extractions.
